premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloys contain a high density of non-equilibrium defects
These defects cause a broad distribution of magnetic exchange interactions
Broad exchange distribution governs the sharp, hysteretic magnetocaloric response
Low-temperature annealing reduces defect density and narrows the exchange distribution
Narrower exchange distribution broadens the magnetocaloric peak and reduces hysteresis
